titre: You can now order the Steam Machine without a reservation, but the 2TB model could be in trouble
chapo: Valve says you can now buy a 512GB Steam Machine with no reservation, but it doesn't have the best news about the 2TB model.

"Add to cart status" has been achieved, which is the most Valve way of saying you can buy one now Valve has issued an update on its Steam Machine stock levels, waiting lists, and purchasing process, saying that the 512GB model has now achieved "add to cart status". After months of joining a lottery-based waiting list to secure the brand's alternative to a gaming PC, you can now grab the entry-level model and its bundled controller with no waiting or reservation constraints. Unfortunately, the same can't be said of the 2TB model, which could even see further price hikes, let alone wait lists. Valve posted an update to its hardware blog yesterday evening, confirming that despite the doom and gloom of the 2TB model, "We've finished getting purchase invites out to all reservation holders." The blog post says, "We've been able to fulfill all current reservations for the 512GB model with no waitlist remaining, and have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders. "However, we are continuing to encounter supply constraints for hardware components, which impacts our ability to source parts." The Steam Machine, along with the Steam Controller and Steam Frame, were all meant to launch in "early 2026", but the very same supply constraints Valve is mentioning this week caused massive delays and (presumably) big price hikes on the company's new generation of hardware. On the 2TB model's future availability, Valve says: "We expect to have more details to share in January about additional supply." But given the RAM shortages that are ongoing, and that SSD prices just keep increasing, it's highly likely that Valve will need to jump the 2TB model's price to even higher ranges in the new year, because the current RAM and SSD situation shows no sign of stopping. "We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them," says Valve. titre: You Can Now Buy the Steam Machine Without a Reservation – But Supplies Are Limited
chapo: Back when the Steam Machine first came out in June, it was in short supply, due to the limited amount of hardware Valve was able to get its hands on (thanks, RAM crisis). But now, about 5 months after launch, you can finally just buy a Steam Machine.
extrait: When the Steam Machine first came out in June, it was in short supply, due to the limited amount of hardware Valve was able to get its hands on (thanks, RAM crisis). Now, about 5 months after launch, you can finally just buy a Steam Machine. Valve put out a blog post on November 19 giving an update on Steam Machine reservations, revealing that it had just finished out sending purchase invites to anyone on the reservation list for the 2TB model. The 512GB version, though, is now available to purchase on the Steam store page without a reservation. However, it looks like Valve doesn't have the components on hand to make the 2TB model available in the same way. According to Valve's blog, the ongoing memory shortage is particularly impacting the 2TB Steam Machine because of its much larger drive. The company says the amount of people on the waitlist for the 2TB Machine exceeds what there were able to make, and while it's going to make more, it's going to be at a limited rate. Still, Valve was able to get through its 512GB Steam Machine waitlist much earlier than expected. When the mini PC launched, some people were placed on the waitlist with an expected order time of 2027. Luckily, the new year hasn't ticked over, and the Machine is now available to buy for anyone that wants it... but there is a possibility that Valve will sell through its entire supply. Valve does say that it's going to continue to build the Machine, but it sounds like the production run is going to be limited. It says that "memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result, we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them." It's no secret that the RAM crisis has been particularly unforgiving to the Steam Machine, and it's not likely to let up in the near future. Samsung told investors in an earnings call last month that it expects supply to be more constrained next year, and all three of the major RAM manufacturers have sold through their manufacturing capacity through next year. It doesn't seem likely that the memory and storage costs that are limiting how many Steam Machines Valve can make will let up at all in the near future.
